18:75.text: said: "Did I not tell you that you can have no patience with me?"

18:76.text: said: "If I ask you anything after this, keep me not in your company, you have received an excuse from me."

18:77.text: Then they both proceeded, till, when they came to the people of a town, they asked them for food, but they refused to entertain them. Then they found therein a wall about to collapse and he
said: If you had wished, surely, you could have taken wages for it!"

18:78.text: said: "This is the parting between me and you, I will tell you the interpretation of
things over which you were unable to hold patience.

18:79.text: "As for the ship, it belonged to Masâkîn
working in the sea. So I wished to make a defective damage in it, as there was a king behind them who seized every ship by force.

18:80.text: "And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared lest he should oppress them by rebellion and disbelief.

18:81.text: "So we intended that their Lord should change him for them for one better in righteousness and nearer to mercy.

18:82.text: "And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the town; and there was under it a treasure belonging to them; and their father was a righteous man, and your Lord intended that they should attain their age of full strength and take out their treasure as a mercy from your Lord. And I did them not of my own accord. That is the interpretation of those
over which you could not hold patience."

18:83.text: And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnain. Say: "I shall recite to you something of his story."
